art_handoff_hint: Art Studio adapts shared pattern settings for composition. Your experiments and observations stay here.
brightness_description: Two gray squares on different backgrounds. Adjust the backgrounds, then compare without them.
brightness_explanation: Both center squares use the same RGB fill. Surrounding light and dark regions can change apparent brightness. The drawing values describe this image, not a calibrated measurement of your display.
brightness_match_description: A fixed gray square on the left and an adjustable gray square on the right. Match their apparent brightness by eye.
brightness_match_result: Left RGB {reference}; right RGB {comparison}. Difference: {difference} RGB-code steps.
cafeWall_description: Alternating dark and light square tiles separated by gray mortar. Shift every second row.
cafeWall_explanation: All mortar bands are horizontal and parallel. Staggered tiles can make the bands look tilted. Try aligned rows or change the mortar width; the strength of the effect may change.
cafeWall_question: How do the horizontal mortar bands look?
cafeWall_result: Every mortar guide has identical start and end height.
comparison_columns_hint: Drawings sit side by side when space allows, and stack on narrower screens. Both use the same scale.
comparison_pinned: Current settings pinned. Adjust the experiment to compare.
comparison_stacked_hint: Each drawing uses the full available width at the same scale.
comparison_switch_hint: Switch between drawings in the same position. Controls and exports use the current experiment; changing a drawing setting brings it into view.
comparison_viewer_hint: Choose trials and guides for A and B independently. Both drawings use the same scale. Saved observations stay unchanged.
delete_saved_study_hint: This removes all {count} retained observations in this saved study. Other observations stay in place. One Undo is available after deleting.
drawing_viewer_hint: Choose a trial and toggle measurement guides. Saved observations stay unchanged.
drawing_viewer_unavailable: The enlarged drawing could not open. You can still inspect it in the recorded drawing panel.
ebbinghaus_description: Orange circles surrounded by different rings of blue circles. Change the surrounding circle size or gap.
ebbinghaus_explanation: The two orange circles keep the same diameter. Size judgments can change with the surrounding circles. Remove the surroundings and compare your impression with the outlines.
ebbinghaus_match_description: A fixed orange circle on the left and an adjustable orange circle on the right. Match their apparent size by eye.
ebbinghaus_question: Which orange center circle looks larger?
equal_scale_hint: Both drawings use the same scale. Matching target values stay hidden in each view until that view is revealed.
export_unavailable: Export could not be created. Try again.
focus_browse_expired: The experiment changed before browsing finished. Choose an experiment again.
focus_browse_hint: Choose another drawing here. Your settings and notes are kept for each experiment.
focus_browse_locked: End the repeated study before choosing another experiment.
focus_hint: In compact view, controls and drawings scroll separately when space allows. Closing this view keeps your drawing, notes, and layout.
focus_unavailable: The focused view could not open. Your experiment is still available in the workspace.
geometry_match_result: Reference: {reference} units; comparison: {comparison} units. Difference: {difference} units ({percent}% of the reference).
guided_capacity: Make room for three new matches by deleting observations you no longer need. Existing observations are kept until you delete them.
guided_collecting: One-setting repeat: the baseline reference and starting positions are preserved. The two studies will be selected for comparison after the third match.
guided_complete: Three new matches recorded. The baseline and new study are selected for comparison. Reveal each study separately when you are ready.
guided_hidden_context: Surroundings are removed in this baseline. Make them visible to compare their effect.
guided_hint: Use this saved study as the baseline. Choose one surrounding setting to change. The reference and three starting positions stay the same.
guided_inactive: Choose a setting that changes the visible surroundings.
guided_invalid_value: Choose a value within the setting range.
guided_plan_expired: The baseline or plan changed. Review the saved study and plan the repeat again; recorded matches remain in the notebook.
guided_ready: The new study changes only this setting. The reference and three starting positions stay fixed.
guided_start_hint: Starting opens this experiment and locks its surroundings for three new matches. Your pinned drawing is kept.
guided_unchanged: Choose a different value or state before starting.
hidden_match_value: {position} percent of adjustment range; drawing values hidden until reveal.
import_capacity: This import needs {count} spaces; {available} are available. Delete observations you no longer need, then preview the file again.
import_empty: This notebook has no observations to add.
import_expired: The notebook changed. Preview the file again before adding observations.
import_group_copies: Overlapping repeated studies will be added as separate copies, keeping their matches together.
import_hidden_hint: Saved reveal states are preserved. Hidden drawing values stay hidden.
import_hint: Preview an exported notebook before adding its observations. Existing observations stay saved; the current drawing and pinned view are kept.
import_json: This file is not valid JSON. Choose an exported Perception Lab notebook.

import_preview_ready: Notebook preview ready. Review the counts before adding observations.
import_read: The file could not be read. Choose it again.
import_records: This notebook contains invalid observations or more than 24 records. No observations were added.

import_unchanged: All observations in this file are already saved.
import_undone: Imported observations removed. The previous notebook is restored.
intro: Explore how an image and its surroundings shape what you see. Make a prediction, change one variable, then reveal the drawing.
match_explanation: The difference records your visual match under these settings. Remove or swap the surroundings to see whether your impression changes. Different people, displays, and viewing conditions can give different matches.
match_hint: Keep the reference fixed. Adjust the right or bottom target until it looks like the reference, then reveal the drawing values.
matching_art_handoff_hint: Art Studio uses the reference gray for both center squares. Your unequal visual match is kept in Perception Lab.
matching_circle_gap_hint: Ring positions stay fixed while you match. The gap setting leaves room for the largest comparison circle.
moire_description: Two line grids overlap. Rotate the second grid or change their shared spacing.
moire_explanation: Moiré bands emerge from overlapping repeated patterns. These larger structures are present in the combined image; they are not merely imagined motion. Hide the second grid to inspect the first.
moire_question: What structure do the overlapping lines suggest?
moire_result: Two grids share a spacing of {spacing} drawing units; their angle is {angle}°.
mullerLyer_description: Two horizontal shafts with different arrowhead arrangements. Adjust the fins while observing the shafts.
mullerLyer_explanation: The horizontal shafts have identical endpoints and lengths. Changing the surrounding fins can change apparent length. The guides measure the shafts, excluding their fins.
mullerLyer_match_description: A fixed horizontal shaft at the top and an adjustable shaft below. Match their apparent length by eye; exclude the fins.
necker_description: A wireframe cube with two possible depth interpretations. Compare it with optional face cues.
necker_explanation: A flat wireframe can support more than one depth interpretation. Face cues are hints added to this drawing; they do not establish a single correct interpretation of the original ambiguous figure.
necker_result: The unshaded drawing has no unique front face.
note_placeholder: What changed when you adjusted the surroundings?
notebook_action_expired: The notebook changed. That observation action is no longer available.
notebook_actions_hint: Pin a saved observation to compare it with your current drawing. Deleting an observation offers one undo; export saves your notebook as JSON.
notebook_empty: Choose an impression and save your first observation.
notebook_group_counts: Studies shown: {shown} of {total}. Retained observations shown: {records}.
notebook_hint: This notebook holds up to 24 observations. New observations need one available space; new three-match studies need three. Existing observations stay until you delete them.
notebook_imported: Import complete. Added to your notebook: {count}. Undo import is available.
notebook_no_matches: No saved observations match these filters. Clear or change the filters to see your notebook.
notebook_no_studies: No repeated studies are saved yet. Use All observations to review individual observations, or start three matches in a matching experiment.
notebook_no_study_matches: No saved studies match these filters. Clear or change the filters to see your studies.
notebook_search_hint: Search visible experiment titles, impressions, and notes. Repeated-study observations stay together when any retained match fits the filters. Hidden drawing values are not searched.
notebook_spaces_needed: This action needs {required} available spaces; {free} remain. Export your notebook or delete observations you no longer need to make room.
notebook_undo_capacity: Undo needs {count} available spaces; {free} remain. No observations were changed.
observation_deleted: Observation deleted. Undo deletion is available.
observation_hint: Record your impression. You can revise it; this is an observation, not a scored test.

pair_hidden: Reveal each study separately to see the comparison. Selecting a study does not reveal its drawing values.
pair_inactive_hint: Surroundings were removed in both studies. Settings marked Inactive did not change the displayed targets.
pair_incomplete: Both studies need three retained matches before they can be compared.

pair_missing_option: Selected study is no longer in the notebook
pair_multiple_changes: Several surrounding settings differ. This comparison does not isolate the effect of one variable.
pair_no_compatible: There is no compatible pair available yet. Both studies need three consistent matches with the same experiment and reference.
pair_plot_hint: Each dot is a trial, top to bottom 1–3; vertical spacing only separates the dots. Horizontal lines show ranges, solid vertical marks show medians, and dashed lines show the fixed reference. Both rows use the same scale.
pair_plot_title: Three matches and the median of each study, on one shared drawing-value scale.
pair_reference: These studies use different fixed references. Repeat the settings with the same reference to compare them.
pair_reference_value: Both studies use the same fixed reference: {value} {unit}.
pair_same_settings: The two studies used the same surrounding settings. Their matches can still vary.
pair_start_changes: These studies used different starting positions. Keep that difference in mind when comparing their matches.
pair_summary_hint: Compare the three matches and ranges as well as the medians. Two small studies describe your matches under these settings; they do not establish a general effect.
pair_table_caption: Separate results from each three-match study
png_exported: Current experiment exported as a 2400 × 1440 PNG.
precision_hint: Exact values apply on Enter or when you leave the field. Escape cancels an edit.
recorded_drawing_hint: Inspect an actual saved match. Trial selections and guides apply only to these previews.
recorded_pair_hint: Inspect trials from each study independently. Both drawings use the same scale; each preview shows its selected recorded match.
reduced_motion_hint: Reduced motion is enabled. Use the crossing-angle slider to compare still frames.
report_not_ready: A report needs complete, consistent, revealed studies. Review the saved results before exporting.
report_print_hint: Open this file in a browser to read or print it. The report includes every recorded trial, independently of the preview selections.
report_unavailable: The study report could not be created. Try again.

setting_invalid: Use a number from {min} to {max}, in steps of {step}. The drawing has not changed.

study_trial_progress: Match {trial} of 3. Adjust the comparison and choose an impression below. Your note is saved with this match; the next match starts with a blank note.

surroundings_swapped: The two surroundings have traded places.
title: Perception Lab
viewing_hint: The viewing area uses a fixed white background to keep comparisons consistent. Different people may notice different effects.
context_cube_hint: Choose a face cue in the controls to compare the cube with and without that cue.
context_comparison_opened: Comparing the same drawing with and without its context. Both views follow your adjustments.
context_comparison_closed: Surroundings comparison closed. Your experiment settings are kept.
context_comparison_hint: Only the context differs. Adjust one setting and compare your impressions. Both drawings follow your adjustments.
context_same_position: Choose Switch views to inspect both drawings in the same position. Changing a drawing setting brings the current experiment into view.
context_tiles_hint: Removing the tiles leaves a flat gray field. Reveal measurements to see horizontal mortar guides in both views.
context_face_hint: The second view adds or removes the selected face cue. The wireframe stays the same; a cue does not establish one correct interpretation.
context_current_only: Save observation and drawing exports use the current experiment in the controls. The second view is a live comparison.
context_pin_kept: Your pinned comparison is kept. Close this comparison to return to it.
match_start_hint: New starting point keeps your settings and note, and clears the previous impression and reveal. Equalize drawing values deliberately makes the comparison equal to the reference. Repeated studies use their own starting points.

match_start_expired: The experiment changed before the starting point was applied. Your latest settings are kept.

inquiry_expired: The experiment changed before the starting view was captured. Your latest settings are kept; capture again when ready.
inquiry_closed: Starting-view comparison closed. Your current settings and saved pin are kept.
inquiry_other_changed: A different setting changed. To explore your chosen setting, return the other setting to its starting value.
inquiry_many_changed: {count} drawing settings changed. Compare one setting at a time to separate their effects.
inquiry_none_changed: No drawing settings changed. Adjust the setting you chose, then compare your impression.
inquiry_hint: Choose a drawing setting and capture a starting view. Adjust that setting, then compare what you see. The starting view stays fixed.
inquiry_cafe_prompt: How does the apparent direction of the mortar bands change?
inquiry_cube_prompt: Which face seems closest, and does that impression stay steady?
inquiry_moire_prompt: What changes in the broad bands compared with the fine lines?
inquiry_comparison_hint: Compare the fixed starting view with your current drawing at the same scale. Switch views to compare them in the same position.
inquiry_hidden_hint: The count describes drawing settings. A hidden grid or face cue may make a setting change invisible. Notes, impressions, and measurement guides are not counted.
inquiry_save_hint: Save observation and SVG/PNG exports use the current drawing. Export inquiry report in the guide keeps both snapshots. The starting view is temporary; your saved pin is kept.
inquiry_scale_hint: Both drawings use the same scale. The starting view keeps the settings captured at that moment.
inquiry_chosen_restored: {setting} returned to its starting value. Your impression and note are kept.
inquiry_others_restored: {count} other drawing settings restored. Your chosen setting, impression, and note are kept.
inquiry_restore_expired: The experiment changed before settings were restored. Your latest settings are kept.
inquiry_restore_hint: Restore chosen setting returns only that setting to its starting value. Restore other settings keeps your chosen setting and returns the other changed settings. Both keep your current impression, note, and measurement guides.
inquiry_report_print_hint: Open this file in a browser to read or print it. Both drawings and observations are fixed snapshots from this inquiry.
inquiry_report_none_changed: No drawing settings changed between these snapshots.
inquiry_report_all_settings: All settings in the two snapshots
inquiry_report_guides_differ: Measurement guide visibility also differs between the two snapshots. This difference is shown in the drawings and settings table, and is excluded from the drawing-setting count.
inquiry_report_interpretation: These snapshots record your drawing settings and observations, not a score or proof of a general effect. A setting change may be invisible or may leave your impression unchanged. Viewing size and displays can affect what you see.
inquiry_report_exported: Inquiry report exported as HTML. Open it in a browser to read or print.
inquiry_report_unavailable: The inquiry report could not be created. Try again.
inquiry_report_hint: Keep both drawings, settings, impressions, and notes in a file you can read or print. The report captures the current visible frame.
ponzo_description: Two orange horizontal bars between perspective rails. Adjust the rails or upper bar position, then compare their apparent lengths.
ponzo_explanation: Both bars have the same drawn length. Converging rails provide a perspective context that can change apparent length. Remove the rails and reveal endpoint guides to compare the drawing. Different people and viewing conditions can give different impressions.
ponzo_result: Both horizontal bars: 240 drawing units. Their horizontal endpoints align.
inquiry_ponzo_prompt: How does the apparent length of the upper bar change when the rails or its position change? Compare again with the rails removed.
context_ponzo_hint: Removing the perspective rails keeps both bars at the same positions and lengths. Reveal measurements to compare their aligned horizontal endpoints.
ponzo_controls_hint: Rail convergence at 0% gives parallel rails. Larger values narrow their upper opening. Increasing Upper bar position moves that bar downward; both bars keep their 240-unit width.
saved_observation_hint: The saved drawing and measurement visibility are preserved.
observation_report_print_hint: Open this file in a browser to read or print. This report preserves the saved drawing, settings, and observation.

observation_review_expired: The saved observation changed or is no longer available. Open its review again.
observation_report_interpretation: This report records one saved drawing and impression. It does not summarize a repeated study. Viewing size and displays can affect the impression.
comparison_slide_hint: Move the divider to inspect both drawings in the same position. This combines parts of two drawings; Switch views shows each complete drawing.
comparison_slide_unavailable: Slide drawings is available when both views use the same experiment.
camera_pan_hint: Turn on Pan drawing to drag. You can also focus a magnified drawing and use Arrow keys; Home fits the whole drawing. Escape turns panning off.
camera_hint: Magnification crops the visible surroundings. Return to Fit whole drawing before comparing your impression. Drawing exports keep the complete current image.
camera_linked_hint: Both drawings use the same magnification and viewing position.
camera_study_locked: Drawing inspection is paused during this study. The whole drawing stays visible.

recorded_camera_hint: Magnification crops the visible surroundings. Return to Fit whole drawing before comparing your impression. Saved drawings and reports stay complete.
pair_plot_heading: Recorded matches on a shared scale
pair_plot_description: Scale {min} to {max} {unit}. Fixed reference {reference}. {studyA}: matches {valuesA}; median {medianA}. {studyB}: matches {valuesB}; median {medianB}.
experiment_preview_hint: Choose a drawing to open its experiment. Previews show the starting drawings; your settings and notes are kept.
camera_crop_reminder: You are viewing part of the drawing. Fit the whole drawing before comparing impressions.
walk_plan_label: Plan of the challenge spaces and your current position
walk_continuity_goal: From the marked viewpoint, move the right rod until both fragments follow the same straight line behind the screen.
walk_continuity_hint_0: Imagine the direction of the left rod continuing behind the screen. Compare that direction with the right rod.
walk_continuity_hint_1: Inspect from another position, then return to the marked viewpoint. Small height changes can make a large difference to the apparent join.
walk_continuity_explanation: An intervening screen can make aligned diagonal fragments appear displaced, as in the Poggendorff illusion. The reveal removes the screen and adds a straight guide from the fixed rod. Your impression may differ from the geometric alignment; this is an exploration, not a vision test.
walk_continuity_plan: Front view of diagonal rods interrupted by a screen
walk_continuity_far: Move closer to the front of the rods.
walk_continuity_view: Return to the marked viewpoint and face the rods before checking.
walk_continuity_again: The fragments are not yet on the same straight line. Compare their direction across the screen.
walk_shadow_goal: Rotate the sculpture until its dark wall silhouette matches the coral outline. Check your match from the marked observation area.
walk_shadow_hint_0: Watch each level of the shadow while turning the sculpture. A small change can expose blocks that were hidden behind others.
walk_shadow_hint_1: Compare the narrow top and the wider lower levels. Walking around the sculpture can help you understand which blocks create each edge.
walk_shadow_explanation: Parallel light paths project the sculpture onto a flat wall. Blocks at different depths can overlap in the shadow, so one silhouette cannot show every part of the solid. The reveal traces the light paths and shows a wireframe orientation that matches the outline.
walk_shadow_plan: Wall silhouette and its target outline
walk_shadow_far: Move closer to the front of the sculpture.
walk_shadow_view: Return to the marked observation area and face the wall before checking.
walk_shadow_again: Some shadow edges still extend beyond the outline or leave gaps. Compare all four levels.
walk_change_goal: Compare both arrangements through the shutter, then identify the object that changed. Solve all three scenes.
walk_change_hint_0: Compare one object at a time across the two arrangements. Its color may stay the same while another property changes.
walk_change_hint_1: Inspect position, height, and orientation. Keeping the same viewpoint can make comparisons easier.
walk_change_explanation: A visual interruption can make a change harder to notice. Comparing the same object across views directs attention to its properties. The outline shows its other arrangement. This untimed exploration is not a test of your attention or vision.
walk_change_plan: Five objects in the current arrangement
walk_change_view: Return to the front observation area and face the display.
walk_change_found: Change found. The next scene is ready.
walk_change_again: That object stayed the same. Compare the two arrangements again.
walk_rotation_goal: Turn and tilt sculptures A and B. Find the one with the same three-dimensional shape as reference R, then solve the second pair.
walk_rotation_hint_0: Follow the chain of blocks from one end to the other. Compare how the bends turn in depth.
walk_rotation_hint_1: Try matching the reference orientation. A mirror image can share a silhouette from one view without being the same solid.
walk_rotation_explanation: Turning a solid changes its viewpoint but preserves its handedness. Each pair contains one rotated copy of R and one mirror image that cannot be made identical by rotation. The gold ring marks the copy; its wireframe shows the reference orientation.
walk_rotation_plan: Reference R and two rotatable block sculptures
walk_rotation_far: Move closer to the front of the sculptures.
walk_rotation_choose: Choose the sculpture with the same shape as R.
walk_rotation_found: Matching copy found. The next pair is ready.
walk_rotation_view: Return to the front observation area and face the sculptures.
walk_rotation_again: That sculpture is a mirror image. Compare how its bends turn in depth.
walk_aperture_goal: Compare the moving rod through the window and with the screen open. Identify its actual motion axis in both trials.
walk_aperture_explanation: Through a small opening, different motions of a diagonal line can produce the same visible change. This ambiguity is called the aperture problem. These two rods follow different motion axes, but their central line occupies the same positions at matching phases. Opening the screen exposes endpoints that distinguish their paths. The reveal traces the actual motion axis.
walk_aperture_hint_0: A short section of a moving line does not reveal every part of its motion. Compare several positions with the screen closed and open.
walk_aperture_hint_1: Follow an endpoint when the screen is open. Does it travel side to side or up and down?
walk_aperture_plan: Perspective view of a moving diagonal rod and aperture screen
walk_aperture_face: Face the rod from an observation area.
walk_aperture_compare: Compare at least two separated positions with the screen closed and open.
walk_aperture_choose: Choose the actual motion axis of the rod.
walk_aperture_found: Motion identified. The next trial is ready.
walk_aperture_again: Follow an endpoint with the screen open and compare its path.
walk_anamorphosis_goal: Move beams B and C until all three fragments form one triangle from the front viewpoint. Record front and side observations of the finished arrangement, then solve the second arrangement.
walk_anamorphosis_hint_0: Compare the endpoints where neighboring fragments should meet. The coral anchor stays fixed while the teal beams move.
walk_anamorphosis_hint_1: Inspect the side viewpoint to reveal the gaps in depth. After adjusting a beam, record both viewpoints again, then return to the front to check.
walk_anamorphosis_explanation: The three fragments occupy different depths. Their endpoints can make one continuous triangle in the image from a particular viewpoint without meeting in space. This viewpoint-dependent construction is called anamorphosis. Moving sideways reveals the depth gaps. Gold outlines show the target positions without moving the actual beams.
walk_anamorphosis_plan: Perspective view of three separated beams
walk_parallax_found: Nearest sphere identified. The next arrangement is ready.
walk_parallax_alternate_explanation: The nearest sphere shifts farthest across the image between straight-ahead sideways viewpoints. Physical sizes change between arrangements to keep their apparent sizes similar at the starting distance, so color and apparent size do not identify the answer. The reveal compares forward distances from the shared baseline.
walk_ring_found: Viewpoint found. The next arrangement is ready.
walk_ring_plan: Circle fragments from your current viewpoint
walk_ring_alternate_explanation: Each arrangement has a different matching viewpoint. The fragments sit on separate depth planes, but rays from one position join their projected endpoints into a circle. The gold marker and rays identify that position; moving away opens the gaps again.
walk_anamorphosis_undone: Beam adjustment undone. Viewpoint observations cleared.
walk_anamorphosis_redone: Beam adjustment restored. Viewpoint observations cleared.
walk_anamorphosis_angular_goal: Turn beams B and C around their fixed pivots until the fragments form one triangle from the front. Record front and side observations, then solve the second arrangement.
walk_anamorphosis_angular_hint_0: Each beam turns around a fixed midpoint. Compare both of its endpoints with the neighboring fragments; a turn that improves one join can worsen the other.
walk_anamorphosis_angular_explanation: Turning the beams changes their orientation without changing their length, midpoint, or depth. Their projected endpoints can align from the front even while they remain separated in space. The side view exposes the gaps; gold outlines show the matching orientations.
walk_anamorphosis_depth_goal: Move beams B and C nearer or farther away until the three fragments form one triangle from the front. Record front and side observations, then solve the second arrangement.
walk_anamorphosis_depth_hint_0: Moving a beam closer makes its image larger; moving it away makes it smaller. Its physical length stays fixed. Compare both endpoints with the coral anchor.
walk_anamorphosis_depth_explanation: Each beam keeps its physical size while sliding in depth. Closer beams make larger images, so the endpoints can align from the front even though the fragments never meet. The side view exposes this separation; gold outlines show the matching depths.
walk_anamorphosis_view_needed: Use a front or side observation viewpoint.
walk_anamorphosis_face: Face the beams from the observation area.
walk_anamorphosis_compare: Record front and side views after your final adjustment.
walk_anamorphosis_front_needed: Return to the front viewpoint to check the joins.
walk_anamorphosis_found: The fragments align. The next arrangement is ready.
walk_anamorphosis_again: The endpoints do not yet meet in the front view.
walk_silhouette_goal: Find the sculpture that matches both reference silhouettes. Compare its front and side views, then solve the second pair.
walk_silhouette_hint_0: The two sculptures share a front silhouette. Their blocks extend differently in depth.
walk_silhouette_hint_1: Turn both sculptures a quarter turn and compare the side reference, including its gaps and levels.
walk_silhouette_explanation: The references use parallel projection, which discards depth: different solids can cast the same outline. A second view supplies more constraints; walking around these perspective sculptures can also reveal their depth. Both candidates match the front reference, but only one matches the side reference. The gold outline identifies that solid. Two views need not determine every possible solid uniquely; these pairs are constructed to have one matching candidate.
walk_silhouette_again: The side silhouette differs. Compare its occupied levels and gaps.
walk_silhouette_compare: Compare the front and side orientations before checking.
walk_silhouette_face: Face the sculptures from the observation area.
walk_silhouette_found: Both views matched. The next pair is ready.
walk_silhouette_plan: Perspective sculptures and their front and side reference silhouettes
walk_length_goal: Match the lower teal shaft to the upper coral shaft in physical length. Compare the current match with the fins shown and hidden, then solve the second arrangement.
walk_length_hint_0: Compare the straight shafts between their endpoints, not the total width including the fins.
walk_length_hint_1: Hide the fins without changing the shaft. A straight-ahead viewpoint can help you compare the endpoints.
walk_length_explanation: Endpoint fins can change how long a shaft appears, a pattern known as the Muller-Lyer illusion. Here, showing or hiding the fins leaves both shaft lengths unchanged. The second trial reverses the fin directions. Gold guides mark the reference endpoints. Your impression may vary; this is an exploration, not a vision test.
walk_length_plan: Perspective comparison of two shafts and their endpoint fins
walk_length_face: Face the shafts from an observation area.
walk_length_compare: Compare the current shaft with the fins shown and hidden.
walk_length_found: Lengths matched. The next arrangement is ready.
walk_length_again: The straight shafts have different lengths. Compare their endpoints.
walk_landing_goal: Lift the three spheres until their shadows cover the floor targets, then solve the second lighting arrangement.
walk_landing_hint_0: Light travels downward to the floor. Raising a sphere shifts its shadow farther from the point directly beneath it.
walk_landing_hint_1: Inspect from the side to compare the sphere and its shadow. A different lighting direction changes where the shadow falls, even if the sphere stays still.
walk_landing_explanation: A cast shadow connects an object with the surface receiving it. Here, parallel light rays project each sphere onto a flat floor. Raising a sphere moves its shadow along the floor without changing the shadow size. Rotating the light here swings the shadows and targets around their spheres without changing sphere heights or shadow size. The reveal traces the light paths and marks the target heights.
walk_landing_plan: Spheres and floor shadows from your current viewpoint
walk_landing_face: Face the spheres from an observation area.
walk_landing_found: Shadows aligned. The next lighting arrangement is ready.
walk_landing_again: Compare each shadow with its floor target.
walk_landing_far: Move closer to the front of the spheres.
walk_weave_goal: Move the three beams to match the crossing order. Record front and side observations of each finished arrangement, then solve the second pattern.
walk_weave_hint_0: At a crossing, the nearer beam hides part of the farther one. Follow each beam away from the crossing to identify it.
walk_weave_hint_1: Inspect from the side to compare the gaps between beams. Moving a beam changes the arrangement, so record both views again after adjusting it.
walk_weave_explanation: Occlusion provides a relative-depth cue: the nearer beam interrupts the visible contour of the farther beam. A front view can hide how far apart the beams are. Moving sideways reveals their separation. The reveal traces their depths along the floor. Many arrangements work; the order and clear separation matter, not one exact position.
walk_weave_plan: Three crossing beams seen from your current viewpoint
walk_weave_view_needed: Use a front or side observation position.
walk_weave_face: Face the beams from an observation area.
walk_weave_observe: Record both a front and a side view of the current arrangement before checking.
walk_weave_found: Crossing order matched. The next pattern is ready.
walk_weave_again: Compare the crossing order and leave a clear gap between each beam.
walk_frame_goal: Align the rod vertically, then horizontally. Compare it with and without the tilted frame in each trial.
walk_frame_hint_0: A tilted surround can change what looks upright. Compare the rod with the frame hidden, without turning the rod.
walk_frame_hint_1: Use the room as a second reference. In the first trial the rod should be vertical; in the second it should be parallel to the floor.
walk_frame_explanation: A tilted frame can influence perceived orientation, a phenomenon called the rod-and-frame illusion. Turning or hiding the surround leaves the rod unchanged. The reveal adds world-space vertical and horizontal references. The effect can vary with the available visual cues; this exploration is not a vision test.
walk_frame_plan: Rod and tilted frame seen from your current viewpoint
walk_frame_view: Face the rod from the front observation area.
walk_frame_compare: Compare the rod with the frame shown and hidden before checking.
walk_frame_found: Alignment found. The horizontal trial is ready.
walk_frame_again: The rod is still tilted from the target direction. Compare it against the room with the frame hidden.
walk_motion_goal: Compare the moving spheres. Select the three that travel together, then solve the second pattern.
walk_motion_hint_0: Compare how the gaps between spheres change as the motion advances. Nearby spheres do not necessarily belong together.
walk_motion_hint_1: The matching three share the same displacement at every moment. Compare at least three separated phases of the motion.
walk_motion_explanation: Elements with shared motion can appear to belong to one group, a cue called common fate. The matching spheres keep the same spacing in three-dimensional space while traveling together. Their color and size do not identify the group. The reveal connects the matching spheres and traces their displacement from the starting positions.
walk_motion_plan: Six spheres at the current motion phase
walk_motion_limit: Three spheres are selected. Unselect one before choosing another.
walk_motion_view: Face the spheres from the front observation area.
walk_motion_observe: Compare at least three separated phases of the motion before checking.
walk_motion_choose: Choose three spheres that travel together.
walk_motion_found: Shared motion found. The next pattern is ready.
walk_motion_again: These spheres do not all travel together. Compare how their spacing changes.
walk_shape_goal: Turn, tilt, and inspect both hoops. Find the true circle, then solve the second pair.
walk_shape_hint_0: A circle can make an oval image when viewed at a slant. The image alone does not tell you the physical shape.
walk_shape_hint_1: Compare each hoop from several directions. Turning changes its projection, but not the lengths of its two principal diameters.
walk_shape_explanation: A slanted circle projects an oval image, even though the hoop remains circular. An oval can also look rounder from some viewpoints. Shape constancy concerns recognizing a stable physical shape across these changing views. The colored diameter guides have equal lengths only on the circular hoop.
walk_shape_plan: Two hoops seen from your current viewpoint
walk_shape_far: Move closer to the front of the hoops.
walk_shape_choose: Choose the hoop whose physical shape is a circle.
walk_shape_found: Circle found. The next pair is ready.
walk_shape_view: Face the hoops from the front or an inspection viewpoint.
walk_shape_retry: That hoop is an oval. Compare its shape from another direction.
walk_relief_goal: Change the lighting above and below the surfaces. Find the hollow surface, then solve the second pair.
walk_relief_hint_0: A bright edge can come from the lighting direction, not just the shape. Compare the same surface under opposite lights.
walk_relief_hint_1: Inspect a surface from the side. Its center stays raised or recessed even when the shading reverses.
walk_relief_explanation: Shading depends on both surface shape and light direction. Expectations about lighting can influence whether a surface looks raised or hollow, but other visual cues also matter. Moving sideways exposes the actual depth; changing the light leaves that depth unchanged. The gold profile compares each surface with its flat rim.
walk_relief_plan: Two shaded surfaces seen from your current viewpoint
walk_relief_view: Face the surfaces from the front or an inspection viewpoint.
walk_relief_both: Compare the surfaces with light from above and below before checking.
walk_relief_choose: Choose the surface with a hollow center.
walk_relief_found: Hollow surface found. The next pair is ready.
walk_relief_again: That surface is raised. Compare its depth from a side viewpoint.
